brief.text:
SITUATION NOW
Floods have inundated roads in southeastern Algeria. [1]
Concern is growing over Algeria's plans to end the moratorium on the death penalty. [2]

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR ALGERIA
Algeria's status as a net energy exporter, with a net energy import dependency of -129%, supports the viability of its new plastic components factory to strengthen the auto industry. [4][E3]

KEY RISKS
Algeria's 14 US OFAC and Canada SEMA sanctions designations pose a risk of increased international isolation or restricted trade. [E2]
The most severe government travel advisory for Algeria is Exercise Increased Caution, indicating risks for travellers and potential reputational concerns. [E1]

WATCH ITEMS
Whether Algeria will proceed with ending the moratorium on the death penalty. [2]
The outcome of the new book examining the roots of the Algeria-France rift. [3]

evidence.label: Net energy import dependency
evidence.factText: Algeria has a net energy import dependency of -129% (World Bank Open Data, 2023); a negative value means Algeria is a net energy exporter.
